cardCompletionMeaning: These are review checklists. completionCondition currently describes acceptance of a rule card, not fulfillment of a case obligation. Executable requirement-specific legal completion predicates must be supplied by the later scoped review.

cards.question: Which facts and reviewed authorities would establish whether this case falls within the intended scope?
cards.scope: Constructed NC conventional residential, full-tenancy-end, cash-deposit, USD examples only; applicability is not established.
requiredFacts: Jurisdiction and tenancy regime
Whether the tenancy ends in full
Deposit type, currency, agreement evidence, and special circumstances
Input origin
consequences: Future review must distinguish missing facts from unsupported scope; this card grants no applicability or live-use approval.
cards.completionCondition: A qualified reviewer documents verified authority, reviewed scope and exclusions, and evidence-backed case facts; this card remains pending until that review.
reconsiderWhen: Agreement, jurisdiction, occupancy regime, tenancy-end scope, deposit type, or governing authority changes
evaluationScenarios: Constructed full residential departure with complete scope facts
Constructed partial roommate departure or uncertain deposit type requiring separate review
unresolvedInterpretations: Source verification and legal review are pending.
Article 6 applicability, exclusions, and special-regime treatment are not verified.

cards.question: What reviewed legal event and accepted evidence establish ACCOUNTING_TRIGGER?
cards.scope: Independent acceptance of the accounting trigger, not automatic selection among case dates.
requiredFacts: Separate NOTICE, INTENDED_DEPARTURE, AGREEMENT_END, VACANCY, KEY_RETURN, and LEGAL_POSSESSION facts with evidence
Separately accepted ACCOUNTING_TRIGGER, accepting party, and reason
Disputed or corrected date evidence
consequences: No automatic maximum-of-dates calculation or missing-invoice exception is authorized.
Without a separately accepted ACCOUNTING_TRIGGER, the synthetic period assumptions do not establish a due date.
cards.completionCondition: A qualified reviewer verifies the G.S. 42-52 accounting reference and trigger interpretation; a separate evidence-backed trigger acceptance identifies its basis and accepting party.
reconsiderWhen: Possession, termination, vacancy, key-return evidence, accepted facts, or reviewed authority changes
evaluationScenarios: Constructed conflicting agreement-end, vacancy, and key-return dates with no automatically selected maximum
Constructed correction to a previously accepted ACCOUNTING_TRIGGER
unresolvedInterpretations: Source verification and legal review are pending.
The legal trigger, date-counting conventions, and effects of disputed possession remain unverified.

cards.question: What reviewed authority and item-specific evidence support responsibility, allowability, amount, and the separate charge choice?
cards.scope: Item-level deposit-deduction review; vendor cost is not automatically a tenant charge.
requiredFacts: Agreement and before/after condition evidence
Causation, responsibility allocation, work scope, and cost version
Supported amount and unresolved questions
Separate chosen or waived amount and decision authority
consequences: Future review must keep vendor cost, allocation, legal allowability, supported amount, and chosen or waived charge distinct.
An invoice alone does not establish tenant responsibility or legal allowability; an unknown amount is not zero.
cards.completionCondition: A qualified reviewer verifies the relevant Article 6 damage provisions and interpretation; item decisions cite supporting evidence and retain unresolved questions rather than inventing amounts.
reconsiderWhen: Condition evidence, responsibility, invoice version, supported amount, charge choice, or reviewed authority changes
evaluationScenarios: Constructed invoice for damage with disputed causation
Constructed supported repair cost with split allocation or a separately waived charge
unresolvedInterpretations: Source verification and legal review are pending.
Relevant Article 6 damage provisions, wear-and-tear treatment, valuation, and deduction limitations are not verified.

cards.question: What ordinary accounting, communication, and money obligations would verified authority require?
cards.scope: Ordinary closeout review; ordinaryPeriodDays = 30 is only a constructed assumption relative to a separately accepted ACCOUNTING_TRIGGER.
requiredFacts: Separately accepted ACCOUNTING_TRIGGER and evidence
Charge decisions, reconciled deposit balance, and prior money events
Statement version, recipient instructions, and performance evidence
Any separately reviewed interim qualification
consequences: The synthetic 30-day assumption does not establish a verified legal deadline or activate a calculation.
Missing invoices do not automatically extend a period or excuse accounting or money obligations.
cards.completionCondition: A qualified reviewer verifies the G.S. 42-52 accounting reference, applicable ordinary duties, timing conventions, and required performance evidence.
reconsiderWhen: Trigger, charge decisions, reconciliation, recipients, performance evidence, or reviewed authority changes
evaluationScenarios: Constructed complete record using the 30-day assumption and an independently accepted trigger
Constructed missing invoice with ordinary obligations still unresolved, not automatically extended
unresolvedInterpretations: Source verification and legal review are pending.
Ordinary duty content, date counting, delivery requirements, and money timing are not verified.

cards.question: What reviewed condition and evidence would qualify the case for an interim accounting path?
cards.scope: Interim qualification is separate from cost uncertainty and interim money handling; UNRESOLVED_PENDING_REVIEW.
requiredFacts: Interim condition state, evidence, and reason
Facts explaining why an amount or extent of a claim is not yet determined
Separately accepted ACCOUNTING_TRIGGER
Item-specific missing facts and available records
consequences: A missing invoice alone does not establish qualification or an automatic exception.
No full withholding, deadline extension, or money disposition follows from this pending card.
cards.completionCondition: A qualified reviewer verifies the relevant G.S. 42-52 accounting reference and qualifying condition, then specifies necessary evidence and exclusions independently of money handling.
reconsiderWhen: Missing evidence arrives, claim uncertainty changes, interim condition is disputed, or reviewed authority changes
evaluationScenarios: Constructed known completed work with only an invoice missing
Constructed disputed extent of damage requiring qualification review rather than automatic interim selection
unresolvedInterpretations: Source verification and legal review are pending.
The qualification test, required explanation, and its relationship to ordinary duties are not verified.

cards.question: What money, if any, must be returned or may be retained during a reviewed interim path?
cards.scope: UNRESOLVED_PENDING_REVIEW; interim qualification does not imply full withholding.
requiredFacts: Separately reviewed interim qualification
Reconciled deposit balance and explicit included transactions
Known chosen deductions and unresolved items
Prior settled refunds, pending requests, reversals, and recipient instructions
possibleAnswers: A money treatment documented by a future qualified review
consequences: Do not assume full withholding, zero refund, or a particular partial refund from uncertainty.
A pending review card authorizes no transfer, reservation, deposit application, or ledger posting.
cards.completionCondition: A qualified reviewer verifies authority and explicitly documents interim money duties, amounts or calculation principles, timing, and evidence requirements; reconciliation and execution remain separate.
reconsiderWhen: Amounts become supported, balance or transaction evidence changes, qualification changes, or reviewed authority changes
evaluationScenarios: Constructed deposit with some supported deductions and one unknown cost, without assuming full retention
Constructed prior refund and pending request requiring reconciliation before any later proposal
unresolvedInterpretations: Source verification and legal review are pending.
Interim return, retention, and timing details remain UNRESOLVED_PENDING_REVIEW; no withholding default is supplied.

cards.question: What final accounting and money obligations follow from a properly reviewed interim path?
cards.scope: finalPeriodDays = 60 is only a constructed assumption relative to the same separately accepted ACCOUNTING_TRIGGER, not to an interim statement date.
requiredFacts: Separately accepted ACCOUNTING_TRIGGER and reviewed interim qualification
Final item decisions and explicit unresolved amounts
Reconciled balance, prior applications, postings, refunds, and pending requests
Final statement version, recipient instructions, and performance evidence
consequences: The synthetic 60-day assumption is not a verified legal deadline, implemented calculation, or automatic ordinary-period extension.
Unresolved amounts must remain explicit; a final statement, approval, or request alone does not prove completed money performance.
cards.completionCondition: A qualified reviewer verifies the G.S. 42-52 accounting reference, final duties, timing and unresolved-claim treatment, and specifies evidence needed to demonstrate performance.
reconsiderWhen: Trigger, qualification, item decisions, reconciliation, recipient instructions, delivery, or money outcomes change
evaluationScenarios: Constructed interim and final examples each anchored to the separately accepted ACCOUNTING_TRIGGER
Constructed unresolved claim at the final assumed period without invented zero amount or automatic further extension
unresolvedInterpretations: Source verification and legal review are pending.
Final duty content, date counting, remaining uncertainty, and corrections are not verified.

cards.question: Who should receive the statement and refund, by which reviewed methods and independently verified instructions?
cards.scope: Statement recipients and refund recipients are separate from ownership, signatory status, and action authority.
requiredFacts: Parties, roles, agreement evidence, and relevant effective periods
Versioned statement and refund recipient instructions with evidence
Disputes, authorized methods, and verified route reference without bank credentials
Separate authority to approve or request the exact action
consequences: Do not infer a refund payee from an owner, manager, custodian, or single signatory role.
An address or authority grant alone does not resolve all recipient questions; no dispatch or payment is performed in Phase A.
cards.completionCondition: A qualified reviewer verifies recipient and method requirements; accepted evidence separately identifies versioned statement and refund instructions and any unresolved disputes.
reconsiderWhen: Recipient instructions, party roles, agreement evidence, authority, route verification, or reviewed authority changes
evaluationScenarios: Constructed multiple signatories with disputed refund instructions
Constructed verified statement destination but unresolved refund recipient
unresolvedInterpretations: Source verification and legal review are pending.
Joint-party entitlement, permissible methods, and the evidence needed for recipient verification are not verified.

cards.question: What reviewed duties and alternatives apply when an address or delivery route is missing or unreliable?
cards.scope: Missing-address details are UNRESOLVED_PENDING_REVIEW; no full-withholding or completed-performance default.
requiredFacts: Which statement or refund route is missing, disputed, or returned
Versioned instructions and evidence of route checks or contact efforts
Separately accepted ACCOUNTING_TRIGGER and pending duties
Money reconciliation and actual communication or money outcomes
possibleAnswers: A missing-address procedure documented by a future qualified review
consequences: A missing address does not itself authorize full withholding, an automatic deadline extension, write-off, or completion.
Contact attempts are evidence of effort, not automatically evidence that communication or money obligations were performed.
cards.completionCondition: A qualified reviewer verifies applicable missing-address duties, permitted alternatives, money treatment, timing, and proof requirements; specific route facts and unresolved issues are documented.
reconsiderWhen: An address is received, a delivery or refund is returned, route reliability changes, or reviewed authority changes
evaluationScenarios: Constructed missing forwarding address without treating the entire deposit as retainable
Constructed returned statement despite a previously recorded address
unresolvedInterpretations: Source verification and legal review are pending.
Missing-address procedures, retention or return details, and timing remain UNRESOLVED_PENDING_REVIEW.

cards.question: What accepted evidence demonstrates each obligation was actually performed, and what later evidence requires reconsideration?
cards.scope: Separate decisions, communications, approvals, money, and related-account tracks; no execution or completion engine in Phase A.
requiredFacts: Exact statement and approval versions, request IDs, payload fingerprints, and authority versions
Dispatch and money result evidence, including returns, failures, and unknown outcomes
Reconciled canonical transactions and reversals
Separate related-task completion evidence
consequences: Preparation, approval, submission, acknowledgement, or effort alone does not demonstrate completed performance.
Unknown results require reconciliation rather than blind retries; returned or reversed results can require reconsideration.
Deposit completion and overall case completion are distinct future determinations, not outputs of these cards.
Legal performance and financial settlement are separate; do not impose check clearance as a universal legal completion condition.
cards.completionCondition: A qualified reviewer verifies obligation-specific legal proof requirements; independently accepted outcome evidence and reconciliation support each relevant track without equating a request to success.
reconsiderWhen: Delivery is returned, a payment fails or reverses, an outcome becomes known, authority is disputed, or related-task evidence changes
evaluationScenarios: Constructed acknowledged refund request with unknown settlement remains unresolved
Constructed returned payment after a previously recorded success prompts reconsideration
Constructed completed deposit tasks with a separate related-account task still open
unresolvedInterpretations: Source verification and legal review are pending.
Legally sufficient proof of communication and money performance, and the effects of later failures, are not verified.
